authority: historical articulation metadata plus bounded perceptual stress-test projection only; not historical phonetic reconstruction, Hebrew pronunciation canon, curriculum authority, identity, recognition, readiness, governance, MANA policy, healing claim, or metaphysical frequency doctrine
purpose: Test whether the five Sefer Yetzirah articulation regions can vary as an auditory surface while the registered Vitae Tree transformation operators remain invariant and independently legible.

historical_reference: Sefer Yetzirah Gra Version 2:3 describes twenty-two foundation letters as engraved with voice, carved with breath, and set in the mouth in five places.
The five cited groupings are throat/guttural, palate/palatal, tongue/lingual, teeth/dental, and lips/labial.
modern_acoustic_reference: Speech-perception research shows that place of articulation can be cued by formant transitions, spectral shape, relative spectral energy, burst/noise properties, and their interaction with phonetic context.
Those findings do not establish one fixed timbre for a historical articulation group and do not reconstruct ancient Hebrew pronunciation.

prototype_signal_architecture.reason: Pitch/frequency and pan encode the Tree transformation operator. Timbre is inserted as an orthogonal spectral-envelope layer and therefore may vary without rewriting the operator coordinates.
prototype_signal_architecture.fundamental_preservation_rule: Every proxy retains an audible fundamental component throughout the operator so a timbre change cannot intentionally erase the pitch trajectory.
prototype_signal_architecture.stereo_preservation_rule: Timbre shaping is applied before the operator pan stage and has no left/right bias.
prototype_signal_architecture.duration_preservation_rule: All proxy comparisons use the same edge duration and amplitude envelope.
prototype_signal_architecture.detune_rule: Timbre proxies may not detune the carrier fundamental or alter the registered 3:2 vertical-step projection.

synthetic_timbre_proxies.posture: Five deliberately synthetic spectral envelopes provide different auditory textures for stress testing only. Their mapping to historical group labels is versioned, replaceable, and has no claim of phonetic accuracy.

operators.semantic_projection: frequency trajectory changes; pan remains centered
frequency remains level; pan crosses the field

structural_acceptance_criteria: Changing timbre profile does not change operator frequency trajectory.
Changing timbre profile does not change operator pan trajectory.
Changing carrier does not change operator class.
Mirroring reverses left/right presentation but not operator class.
Audio-off plain-language output names the same operator independently of all sound settings.
human_perception_acceptance_criteria: A listener can distinguish vertical, horizontal, and diagonal operators above chance across multiple timbre profiles without relying on station labels.
No single timbre profile is required for operator recognition.
Reduced-sensory and audio-off modes convey equivalent relation identity.

fivefold_vitae_boundary.reason: The two fivefold structures arise from different source grammars. Count equality alone does not justify element-to-articulation correspondence.

candidate_laws: Articulation Region Is Not Timbre Identity — a historical production grouping may guide a perceptual family without claiming one invariant sound signature.
Timbre May Color an Operator; It May Not Rewrite It.
Fundamental and Pan Preserve Relation — the operator-defining trajectories remain stable while spectral envelope varies.
Fivefold Is Not Fivefold Identity — equal cardinality between articulation groups and Vitae section modes creates no correspondence by itself.
Proxy Before Reconstruction — synthetic timbres must remain explicitly experimental until historically and phonetically grounded recordings or models exist.
Human Perception Must Be Measured — code-level orthogonality is necessary but does not prove listener-level recognizability.
